description: Central catalog of all player-visible inventory items (money, costumes, player-card parts, equipment, voice/pose unlocks, characters and story extras), defining their display text, type, cross-table link, stock rules, ordering, and progress unlock gate.

Id.technical: FName row key used by stock counts, shop purchases, unlock checks, reward grants, and inventory-wide row collection. Consumers search all ItemDataTables and use the first matching row. Many joins go the other way too: CharacterVariation::Id_Item, ItemSet::Id_Item, and shop set contents name this ID. The export includes MONEY and ITM_* keys.

Id_ItemText.simple: Localized name/text key for the item.
Id_ItemText.technical: FName passed through GameItem_GetNameTextCore with the row's ItemType. Most types use the key directly; Costume/CustomVoice/SituationOverviewPose substitute fixed template keys and pass this key as an ITEM_NAME text parameter, while Nickname keys are rewritten for the current language's TOP/BOTTOM suffix. None yields an empty/invalid name request in several UI paths. Some title/nickname player-card rows also read the parallel tables' Id_ItemText for labels.

ItemType.technical: EGameItemType (None=0, Money, ShortStory, Costume, Title, Nickname, Emblem, Plate, CursedTools, CursedObjects, Extras, CustomVoice, SituationOverviewPose, StoryDemoMovie, Character, Invalid=255), default None. It drives collection filtering, shop category grouping, icon sprite selection, previewability, money handling, ownership joins, and item-description behavior. Examples: Title..Plate are treated as player-card parts; CursedTools..Extras resolve equipment effects; Extras consume on one-shot use; Money bypasses per-item stock and uses user money.

VariableId.simple: Type-dependent foreign key to the concrete asset/definition behind this item.
VariableId.technical: FName whose target table depends on ItemType. CursedTools/CursedObjects/Extras resolve EquipmentItemDataTable by VariableId, then its effects. Plate and Emblem resolve PlayerCardPlate/PlayerCardEmblem rows. CustomVoice resolves CharacterCustomVoice; SituationOverviewPose resolves its pose table; costume/pose/voice ownership searches match VariableId against variation/voice IDs. None is common for types without a secondary definition. Shared helpers also find the first Item row with a given VariableId.

SortingOrder.technical: int32 at row offset 0x24, default 0. Used to stable-sort collection archive tiles/text rows and player-card title/nickname items, to order the first item of a shop set's lineup, and to sort vs-enemy equipment tabs (usable, used-up, unowned). Exported values are mostly unique and start around 1000; some special rows use 0.

SellPrice.technical: int32 serialized at row offset 0x28 with constructor default 0; exported values are 0, 2000, and 7000. No identifiable C++ consumer reads this field in the available Source, and ShopLineupDataTable carries its own Price for purchases, so no sale formula or currency interaction can be asserted.

PossessionMax.simple: Maximum number of this item the player can hold.
PossessionMax.technical: int32 at row offset 0x2C, default 0. Purchase, initial-grant, and max-possession helpers clamp StudioItemStocks counts with FMath::Min(Count + Amount, PossessionMax). Shop confirm dialogs copy the first set item's value to set purchase quantity limits and disable buttons when stock reaches it; lottery conversion marks a draw replaced when the first item is at max. The MONEY row uses -1 and is handled through user money instead of item stock.

InitialPossession.simple: Amount granted automatically on a fresh/reset save.
InitialPossession.technical: int32 at row offset 0x30, default 0. GameItem_GetInitialRows keeps rows with a positive value; GameItem_GrantInitialItems adds that amount to user money for Money rows or clamps it into StudioItemStocks for others. Shop UI also treats rows with UserProgressFlag < 0 and InitialPossession <= 0 as non-default/available-to-buy items in several availability checks.

UserProgressFlag.simple: Save-data progress bit that unlocks the item.
UserProgressFlag.technical: int32 at row offset 0x34, default 0. Values below 0 mean no gate (unlocked); otherwise the flag encodes UserProgressFlagWords[Flag >> 2] bit (Flag & 3), with word indices >=128 treated as unreached. GameItem_IsRowUnlocked, GameItem_IsUnlocked, collection lists, and shop progress checks all apply this same test. Exported rows use -1, 6, 7, and several other DLC/progress flags.

notes: The export contains 2775 rows. ItemDataTables can contain multiple shards; most helpers scan them in order and use the first matching row. Because names are global inventory keys, duplicate IDs across shards can shadow later rows.

ItemDataTable is a hub: ItemSetDataTable::Id_Item points here; VariableId points outward to EquipmentItem/PlayerCard/Voice/Pose tables; CharacterVariation::Id_Item points back here. Shop unlock and reward code frequently resolves an ItemSet first and then reads the first contained Item row.
SellPrice is serialized but has no identified consumer. No Blueprint behavior is assumed; the reconstruction's source states Blueprints contain no game logic.
Only the supplied retail export and partial Content are available; no claim is made about all retail rows, DLC-specific tables, or editor-only consumers.

usages.detail: Filters owned stock entries by ItemType for inventory/player-card lists.
Grants InitialPossession amounts and clamps them by PossessionMax.
Builds the item name request from Id_ItemText and ItemType.
Chooses item icons by ItemType and resolves VariableId-linked plate/voice/pose art.
Uses VariableId to find EquipmentItem rows and their gameplay effects.
Filters unlocked rows by type and sorts by SortingOrder.
Applies the item progress gate, purchase clamp, and first-item SortingOrder/PossessionMax for shop sets.
